name: The Thinker
kicker: Auguste Rodin’s bronze sculpture · A seated man caught mid-thought
briefing: Auguste Rodin first planned this bronze figure to crown a sculpted doorway called _The Gates of Hell_, brooding over the souls of Dante’s _Inferno_ far below. Rodin’s assistant later enlarged him to his famous six-foot size, and the hunched, muscular pose came to stand for deep thought everywhere, not just one poet’s nightmare. A cast of this very statue now marks Rodin’s own grave.

tossups.p: A cast of this sculpture marks its creator’s own grave at Meudon, outside Paris. Originally meant to depict a brooding poet, it was planned to crown the doorway of the same sculptor’s _Gates of Hell_, gazing down at sinners from Dante’s _Inferno_.
tossups.r: Henri Lebossé later enlarged it to its famous six-foot size. For 10 points, name this bronze sculpture of a seated, muscular man resting his chin on his hand, by Auguste Rodin.

tossups.p: A fanatic named Poitron damaged a cast of this sculpture outside the Panthéon in Paris in the early 1900s, and a different cast at the Cleveland Museum of Art lost its lower legs to a 1970 bombing. Critics have compared its pose to Michelangelo’s statue of Lorenzo de’ Medici.
tossups.r: One cast of this sculpture, made by the lost-wax method, traveled from the 1904 St. Louis World’s Fair to the University of Louisville. For 10 points, name this Auguste Rodin sculpture.

tossups.p: Edvard Munch painted this sculpture standing in Max Linde’s garden, and the photographer Edward Steichen once photographed its own creator posing in front of it in the same hunched position. Early versions of this sculpture showed its subject wearing a small Florentine cap.
tossups.r: It was originally conceived to represent a poet, Dante, brooding over his own _Inferno_. For 10 points, name this bronze and marble sculpture of a seated man, chin on hand, by Auguste Rodin.

tossups.p: French official Edmond Turquet commissioned this sculpture’s creator to design a doorway for a planned museum of decorative arts in 1880; this figure was meant to crown that doorway, brooding over the sinners below. Its twisted pose rests the right elbow on the left thigh.
tossups.r: Henri Lebossé enlarged the original version into the roughly six-foot bronze most museums display today. For 10 points, name this Auguste Rodin sculpture of a muscular, seated man.

tossups.p: A cast of this sculpture once stood outside the Panthéon in Paris before being damaged by a man named Poitron and later moved to the Musée Rodin. This figure was originally meant to represent Dante as a poet, gazing down from a doorway at the souls of Rodin’s _Gates of Hell_.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this bronze sculpture, originally known by another title, showing a muscular man seated on a rock with his chin resting on his hand.

tossups.p: Rodin’s assistant Henri Lebossé enlarged this originally small figure into the roughly six-foot bronze now displayed around the world. One cast, made by the lost-wax process, traveled from the 1904 St. Louis World’s Fair to its permanent home at the University of Louisville.

tossups.r: Rodin originally conceived it to represent a poet, meant to sit above the doorway of his _Gates of Hell_. For 10 points, name this bronze sculpture of a brooding, muscular man.

tossups.p: A 1970 bombing tore the lower legs off a cast of this sculpture at the Cleveland Museum of Art. Decades earlier, an angry man named Poitron had already damaged a different cast of it outside the Panthéon in Paris.

tossups.p: This sculpture was commissioned in 1880 as part of a doorway for a museum that was never built, a doorway its sculptor titled _The Gates of Hell_. Early casts of this smaller, original figure showed it wearing a Florentine cap.

tossups.p: Norwegian painter Edvard Munch once painted this sculpture as it stood in a garden belonging to the collector Max Linde. This sculpture’s twisted pose, with one elbow crossing to the opposite thigh, has often been compared to a seated Medici tomb figure by Michelangelo.
tossups.r: Auguste Rodin first conceived this work to picture Dante, brooding over his own _Inferno_. For 10 points, name this bronze sculpture of a seated man lost in thought.

tossups.p: The photographer Edward Steichen once posed Rodin in front of this sculpture, mirroring its own hunched posture. This figure was originally planned to crown Rodin’s sculpted doorway _The Gates of Hell_, representing Dante looking down at his _Inferno_.

tossups.p: A lost-wax cast of this sculpture traveled from the 1904 World’s Fair in St. Louis to its permanent home at the University of Louisville. A cast outside the Panthéon in Paris was later damaged by a vandal named Poitron.
tossups.r: This muscular, seated figure rests its chin on its hand, a pose Rodin first conceived to represent a poet. For 10 points, name this bronze sculpture by Auguste Rodin.

tossups.r: A cast of this work also sits over its own sculptor’s grave at Meudon, outside Paris. For 10 points, name this Rodin sculpture of a brooding, muscular man, chin on hand.

trap.title: Sculpture, not sculptor or doorway
trap.body: Every clue names Auguste Rodin, so it’s tempting to shout the sculptor’s name instead of the sculpture’s title. There’s a second trap, too: this figure was first conceived for Rodin’s sculpted doorway _The Gates of Hell_, so real tossups often prompt if you buzz with that title too early, before it’s clear they want the seated figure itself.
trap.fix: Listen for “this sculpture” or “this figure” describing a seated man — that wants _The Thinker_, not Rodin, and not the whole doorway it once crowned.
trap.line: Real answer line: The Thinker [or Le Penseur; prompt on The Gates of Hell before mention]
